▪Bradycardia = longer

and possibly put patient in danger 
of life-threatening rhythm

QT interval is 10 small blocks, 10 x 0.04 = 0.40 seconds

records.sourceText:
Copyright © 2017, 2011, 2006 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved
Sinus Pause
• Definition: A brief delay in the SA node's firing, typically lasting less 
than 3 seconds. 
• ECG Finding: The next P wave appears on time or with a slight 
delay, but the overall rhythm is preserved. 
• Clinical Significance: Often benign, especially in young or athletic 
individuals. May go unnoticed. 
• Cause: Can be due to increased vagal tone, medications (e.g., beta 
blockers), or intrinsic SA node dysfunction.

records.recommendation: Sinus Arrest definition, ECG finding, significance and causes. Preserve as source explanation.
records.sourceText:
Copyright © 2017, 2011, 2006 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved
Sinus Arrest
• Definition: A longer and more irregular pause in SA node activity, 
usually greater than 3 seconds.
• ECG Finding: The next P wave is late or absent, and the pause is 
not a multiple of the normal P–P interval.
• Clinical Significance: More serious; may lead to syncope, escape 
rhythms, or even asystole if no backup pacemaker takes over.
• Cause: Often due to sick sinus syndrome, ischemia, fibrosis, or drug 
effects.

records.sourceText:
Copyright © 2017, 2011, 2006 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved
Supraventricular Tachycardia
• Originates ABOVE the ventricles, typically in the 
SA, atria or the atrioventricular (AV) node.
• SVT can result in palpitations, dizziness, shortness 
of breath, or chest discomfort, and may be 
characterized by a sudden onset and termination. 
(Paroxysmal) SVT
• Causes include:
– Lifestyle  (Stress, Caffeine, Intense Physical Exercise)
– Medical Conditions (Structural, Congenital)
– Electrical Disturbances (Congenital, Medications)

records.sourceText:
Copyright © 2017, 2011, 2006 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved
Supraventricular Tachycardia
• Regular, narrow complex tachycardia, with QRS 
duration typically less than 0.12 sec.
• P waves may be absent, buried in the preceding T 
wave, or difficult to distinguish due to the rapid 
rate.
• The ventricular rate is generally between 150 and 
250 beats per minute.
